estimator.name: measureLibrationHarmonic (js/lab3d/libration.js)
estimator.why: The first gate's estimator counts turning points of a smoothed argument. On the authentic argument the osculating ripple is larger than the libration, and no smoothing span made the turning points repeatable (L1, L1s). A tapered least-squares line does not need the ripple removed: terms far from the line in frequency are suppressed by the taper.
estimator.model: phi(t) = c0 + c1 (t - tm) + a cos w (t - tm) + b sin w (t - tm) on the unwrapped argument, tm the middle of the window, by weighted least squares with Hann weights over the window. w is the minimum of the weighted residual sum of squares, scanned at frequencies from 0.5 / W to maxPeriods / W in steps of 1 / (8 W) (W the window) and refined by a golden-section search between the neighbouring scan points.
estimator.options: requiredPeriods = 3 (unchanged from the first gate); maxPeriods = 8 (the line sought completes between 3 and 8 turns in the window; a faster line is ripple to this estimator and belongs to the turning-point estimator); significance = 5; repeatability: sub-windows of the first and the last two thirds of the window.
estimator.refusals: circulation when the net change of the unwrapped argument, smoothed over the conjunction cycle, is 355 deg or more (the first gate's rule). not-constrained, with no period, amplitude or centre: (window-too-short) the minimising period is longer than W / requiredPeriods; (no-line) the amplitude is below `significance` times its formal sigma; (drifting-center) |c1| W exceeds twice the amplitude; (not-repeatable) the two sub-window fits, each a golden-section minimum within 25% of the full-window frequency, differ from each other by more than 25% of the period, or either amplitude is outside half to twice the full-window amplitude.
estimator.values: period 2 pi / w; amplitude hypot(a, b); centre c0 wrapped to [0, 360).
estimator.uncertainty: Formal covariance: the sandwich (J'WJ)^-1 (J'W^2 J) (J'WJ)^-1 (S0 / dt) with J the Jacobian of the model in (c0, c1, a, b, w), W the Hann weights, dt the mean sample spacing and S0 the noise floor near the line: the median, divided by ln 2, of the Hann periodogram ordinates dt |sum w r exp(-2 pi i f t)|^2 / sum w^2 of the residual r at the 24 frequencies f0 + m / W, m = 3..26 (those below the Nyquist frequency). sigma_P = hypot(P^2 sigma_w / (2 pi), half the difference of the two sub-window periods, the sampling floor); sigma_A = hypot(formal, half the difference of the two sub-window amplitudes). A coverage interval is +-2 sigma.
estimator.limits: One line. A libration faster than W / maxPeriods is not looked for. Lines closer than two cycles per window to the fitted one are not separated from it (for the JUP365 window: periods between 1,381 d and 4,142 d). The noise floor is read above the line in frequency and so does not see slower terms.

stepBudget.name: stepForBudget (js/lab3d/stepBudget.js)
stepBudget.why: The first gate committed fixed steps (AM1) that turned out too coarse; AM4 and AM5 then found finer ones by trial. A step is now derived from the error the measurement can afford.
stepBudget.rule: Pilot: the system is advanced from its initial state for pilotPeriods = 50 periods of the innermost body with the kernel's yoshida4 at h0 = innerPeriod / 64, at h0 / 2 and at h0 / 4. Energy error at h0: the largest of E(h0), 16 E(h0/2), 256 E(h0/4), E the largest |dE/E| seen at the ends of the inner periods. Angle error rate of each budgeted angle at h0: (16/15) max(d1, 16 d2) / Tpilot, d1 the largest circular difference between the h0 and h0/2 runs at the ends of the inner periods and d2 the same between h0/2 and h0/4. Prediction at step h over the window: energy E(h0) (h/h0)^4; angle sum_i weight_i rate_i window (h/h0)^4. The step is the largest h <= h0 that divides the sampling interval and whose predictions are at most safety = 0.1 of each budget. If that needs more than 4,096 steps per inner period the budget is refused (not-attainable, no step).
